videos.script: Two questions are left about where pods go. The first: how evenly should copies be spread across zones? Anti-affinity can only say one per zone, which stops working the moment you want more copies than you have zones. {{spread}} A topology spread constraint says something more useful: spread them, and never let one zone get more than this many ahead of another. {{skew}} The second question is what happens when the cluster is full. A priority class ranks pods, and a pod that matters more can push out one that matters less. {{priority}} You will spread six copies across two zones, add a seventh, and then fill the cluster with batch work and watch the checkout service take its place. {{plan}}
